Add the units column, including the carry: 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. Finally, add the tens column: 8 + 1 = 9.

Add tenths column: 3 + 7 + 5 + 1 (carry) = 16 (write 6, carry 1).

questions.hint: Borrow 1 from the tenths digit (6) to subtract 8 from 5 in the hundredths column.

Subtract units (3 - 7 requires borrowing from tens, so 13 - 7 = 6). Subtract tens: 5 - 1 = 4.

questions.hint: Line up the decimal points and perform vertical subtraction, borrowing where necessary.

steps.explain: Align the numbers vertically.
Subtract cents column: 7 - 8 requires borrowing (17 - 8 = 9). 3 - 1 = 2.

questions.hint: Set up subtraction vertically, and borrow from the units digit (8) to subtract the tenths digit.

Subtract hundredths column: 5 - 3 = 2.
Borrow 1 unit from units place (8 becomes 7) to make 13 tenths. Subtract: 13 - 9 = 4.
Subtract units (7 - 4 = 3) and tens (6 - 1 = 5).

questions.hint: Borrow 1 from the tenths digit (2) to subtract the hundredths column.

Subtract units: 7 - 3 = 4. Subtract tens (borrowing from hundreds): 15 - 6 = 9. Hundreds: 2.

questions.hint: Set up subtraction vertically. You will need to borrow in both the hundredths and units columns.

Borrow from tens (9 becomes 8) to make 16 units. Subtract: 16 - 8 = 8. Subtract tens: 8 - 3 = 5. Subtract hundreds: 4 - 1 = 3.

Subtract units (1 - 6 requires borrowing, so 11 - 6 = 5). Subtract tens: 6 - 1 = 5.

questions.stem: A logistics courier has a daily budget of \\(\$50.00\\) for dispatch expenses. They spend \\(\$18.35\\) on fuel refills, \\(\$8.49\\) on road tolls, and \\(\$4.38\\) on package sealing tape. How much of the daily budget remains?
questions.hint: Find the total amount spent by adding the three individual expenses together, then subtract this total from the initial budget of \\(\$50.00\\).

steps.explain: First, identify the initial budget and list all the individual expenses. The initial budget is \\(\$50.00\\), and the expenses are \\(\$18.35\\), \\(\$8.49\\), and \\(\$4.38\\).
Add the three expenses together to find the total amount spent. Align the decimal points vertically to ensure accurate addition of cents and dollars.
Subtract the total expenses of \\(\$31.22\\) from the initial budget of \\(\$50.00\\) to determine the remaining amount. Again, align the decimal points and perform the subtraction.
Verify that the final calculated difference represents the remaining budget. The logistics courier has \\(\$18.78\\) left in their daily budget.

questions.stem: An environmental volunteer team allocates a budget of \\(\$20.00\\) for planting supplies. A volunteer spends \\(\$1.68\\) on biodegradable seed bags, \\(\$3.45\\) on organic fertilizer tablets, and \\(70\\) cents on compost labels. How much budget remains?
questions.hint: Ensure all values are in the same currency unit. Note that \\(70\\) cents is equivalent to \\(\$0.70\\). Sum the expenses and subtract from \\(\$20.00\\).

steps.explain: Identify the starting budget and convert the 70 cents expense into dollars so that all quantities are in the same unit. This is necessary before performing any addition.
Add all three individual expenses together. Make sure to align the decimal points: \\(\$1.68\\) for seed bags, \\(\$3.45\\) for fertilizer, and \\(\$0.70\\) for labels.
Subtract the total spent of \\(\$5.83\\) from the initial budget of \\(\$20.00\\). Align the decimal points and perform the subtraction.
Confirm the remaining budget in dollars. The environmental volunteer team has \\(\$14.17\\) remaining.

questions.hint: Multiply the hourly charge rate of \\(\$7.42\\) by the total duration of \\(35\\) hours.

Set up the multiplication of the decimal number \\(7.42\\) and the whole number \\(35\\).
Multiply the digits: \\(742 \\times 35 = 25970\\). Since the factor 7.42 has two decimal places, place the decimal point two digits from the right of 25970.

questions.hint: Divide the whole number part first (6 / 2), then the decimal part (8 tenths / 2). Keep the decimal point in line.

questions.hint: Divide by 12. Check how many times 12 goes into 104 first.

questions.stem: An industrial warehouse robot traverses a distance of \\(16.47\\) metres in \\(9\\) seconds. At this constant speed, how many metres will the robot travel in exactly one minute?
